A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Go-with-the-Flow research work and complete 22-page documents, including supplementary Sections 6–12. Text and rendered pages match throughout except for the first-page project address and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v4 reports original noise-warping benchmarks, video-generation experiments, ablations and a 40-participant user study, including Tables 1–2 and supplementary Figure 15.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results, ablations and user-study outcomes in Tables 1–2 and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, warped-noise generation, noise degradation, diffusion fine-tuning and inference are identical. Supplementary Figure 17 retains the same pseudocode.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including the general-purpose training videos, WebVid, DAVIS, VIPSeg, DL3DV, WonderJourney and portrait relighting. The same object-control, camera-control, motion-transfer and editing scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator membership within every experiment. Qualitative comparisons also retain their methods, including AnyV2V and MotionClone for first-frame editing in Figure 10.

E3.justification: Training budgets, preprocessing, evaluation metrics and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 43-video DAVIS, 100-video DL3DV and 19-video WonderJourney evaluations and the same 40-participant study design.

E4.justification: The noise-degradation, training-data-size and base-model ablations in Section 4.4.3 are identical. Supplementary analyses of Gaussianity, the windmill example and generation without fine-tuning are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same Gaussianity tests and p-value reporting in Table 1 and user-study statistics in Figure 15. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2, user-study outcomes and qualitative results match, including the supplementary figures. No result is added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–2, their assumptions and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Supplementary Section 6 retains the identical Gaussianity proof and expansion–contraction recovery example.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about efficient Gaussianity-preserving noise warping and model-agnostic motion control. The stated contributions and their scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of motion control, visual quality and baseline behavior are unchanged. Supplementary Sections 8–9 retain the same mechanism explanations and qualification about artifacts without fine-tuning.

D1.justification: The first-page project address and hyperlink change from eyeline-research.github.io/Go-with-the-Flow/ to eyeline-labs.github.io/Go-with-the-Flow/. Implementation details, pseudocode and code/checkpoint links remain unchanged; no new resource availability is documented.

R1.justification: All 75 references and the related-work discussion are identical. Positioning relative to earlier noise-warping and motion-control methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page project-link text and arXiv stamp are updated, from v4 dated 25 March 2025 to v5 dated 6 August 2025. Body prose, headings and document organization are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–17, Tables 1–2, captions and placement are unchanged. Pages 2–22 render identically; page 1 differs only in the substituted project-address and version/date text, without document reflow.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, theory, explanations and supplementary material are identical. The first-page address and version-stamp updates do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or decline; the PDFs do not establish whether the new address improves resource access.
